title: Whether a Lead-share bar was ever the right target

completion_criteria.text: The 50 percent bar's origin is traced to the decision that set it, and what it was meant to detect is stated in that decision's own words rather than reconstructed after the fact.
The Lead share the architecture should produce BY DESIGN is derived from the roster's dispatch topology - a Lead that fans out to N makers implies a share - rather than assumed or asserted.
Whether a share statistic is diagnostic of delegation health at all is settled on evidence; retiring the measure entirely is an allowed and equally valid outcome.
A replacement target, or the decision to have none, is pinned BEFORE any corpus is re-read, so the conclusion cannot be fitted to the measured 24.23 to 26.60 percent.
The measured 24.23 to 26.60 percent is interpreted against whatever is settled, with the struck c5's negative outcome left standing regardless of what that interpretation concludes.

spine.active_goal: Answered. A share statistic is not diagnostic of routing quality, and the routing fix is agent description text rather than measurement.
spine.next_step: Only c1 remains and it is a single read: open decision 0579 and state, in its own words, what the retired bar was trying to detect - that concern may still be real even though its instrument was wrong. Do NOT propose a replacement metric, a dispatch-counting hook, a validator or a Lead budget; 0613 rules all of them out.
spine.last_session: User stopped the measurement Lead mid-flight and ruled the whole approach out. c2, c4 and c5 struck. An implementer is shipping the actual fix: a stopping condition on architect plus when-NOT-to-use clauses on the Leads.

open_risks.text: Never let this thread's conclusion reach back into the struck c5 — re-examining a bar after seeing the number that failed it is post-hoc grading, and c5's negative stands whatever is concluded here

Note that a Lead outnumbering its makers may be the unhealthy shape, not the healthy one — a fan-out tree implies makers exceed Leads by construction, so a greater-than-50-percent target may have inverted the sign it meant to test
Point every observer query at ~/.claude/observer/events and never at ~/.claude/agent-ledger — the retired store has a different schema and answers plausibly

key_decisions.title: Retire Lead share as the target: it is a marginal statistic and routing appropriateness is conditional
Drop the routing measurement entirely: fix triggering with agent description text, not machinery

out_of_scope: Re-measuring Lead share at a new grain, a new Lead set or a new corpus in order to obtain a different number - the measurement is settled and the instrument is shipped.

The filed observer-audit findings - unpaired_stops, the NULL-blind mixed-type halt, the built-ins classification gap that guarantees a halt on any corpus containing one. They are instrument work, not target-design work.
